question: Removing any one side of the fire triangle — fuel, oxygen, or heat — will:
explanation: The fire triangle requires all three elements (fuel, oxygen, and heat) to sustain combustion; removing any one of them will stop the reaction.

question: As pressure is applied to a Bourdon tube, the curved tube tends to:

options.B: Straighten and move the linked pointer
options.D: Generate an electric current in a wire

explanation: An internal C-shaped Bourdon tube has an elliptical cross-section that tends to straighten out under pressure, moving the connected linkage and pointer.

question: The plant logbook is considered:
explanation: The operating logbook serves as an official legal and historical record of plant readings, routine tests, and shift events.

question: No real machine is 100% efficient because some input energy is always lost to:
explanation: In any real mechanical system, friction between moving parts converts a portion of the input energy into thermal energy (heat).

question: To protect a boiler from oxygen pitting, the feedwater system includes a:
explanation: A deaerator uses thermal and mechanical action to strip corrosive dissolved oxygen and carbon dioxide out of the boiler feedwater.

question: Balanced draft in a boiler is achieved by using:

options.B: Natural draft from the chimney stack only
options.C: Both a forced-draft and induced-draft fan

explanation: A balanced draft system employs both a forced-draft (FD) fan to push air in and an induced-draft (ID) fan to pull flue gases out, maintaining a slightly negative pressure inside the furnace.

question: Plant effluent (wastewater) must be treated before discharge to:

options.A: Raise the temperature of the feedwater

explanation: Wastewater treatment is mandatory to ensure discharge meets strict environmental standards and contaminant limits set by regulatory authorities.

question: The defining feature of a firetube boiler is that:

options.A: It has no tubes at all
options.B: Hot gases flow in the tubes, water around them
options.C: The water flows inside the boiler heating tubes
options.D: It is unable to make steam

explanation: In firetube boilers, combustion gases pass through the inside of the tubes, while the boiler water surrounds the outside of the tubes.

question: The lower drum of a watertube boiler that collects sediment is the:
explanation: The mud drum (or lower drum) is located at the lowest point of the circulation loop where suspended solids and sludge naturally settle out.

question: For a service requiring full, unobstructed flow when open and tight shut-off when closed, the best choice is a:
explanation: Gate valves are designed for isolation service (fully open or fully closed), offering minimal flow resistance when open.

question: Boiler drum cover plates are placed inside the drum so that:

options.B: They can be removed while still running normally
options.C: They add strength to the shell
options.D: Internal pressure pushes them tighter to seat

explanation: Placing manhole and handhole covers on the inside ensures that internal boiler pressure acts to force the cover tighter against its sealing gasket.

question: With a latent heat of vaporization of 2250 kJ/kg, evaporating 4 kg of water at its boiling point requires:
explanation: Heat required = $\text{Mass} \times \text{Latent Heat} = 4 \text{ kg} \times 2250 \text{ kJ/kg} = 9000 \text{ kJ}$.

question: The correct extinguisher for a fire in energized electrical equipment is a:
explanation: Class C fire extinguishers use non-conductive agents suitable for fires involving energized electrical equipment.

question: A boiler pressure gauge reads most accurately when the pointer is:
explanation: Bourdon tube pressure gauges provide the highest accuracy and least mechanical wear when operating near the middle of their scale range.

question: Information on the safe handling and hazards of a chemical is found on its:
explanation: A Safety Data Sheet (SDS) provides comprehensive details on chemical properties, health hazards, and protective handling procedures.

question: A compact firetube boiler used aboard ships and in many packaged plants is the:
explanation: The Scotch marine boiler is a self-contained, compact horizontal firetube design traditionally used in marine applications and industrial packaged units.

question: Before anyone enters a boiler drum for inspection, the atmosphere must be:

options.A: Tested for gases, with an entry permit issued
options.D: Gradually heated to full operating temperature

explanation: Pre-entry requirements for confined spaces like boiler drums mandate atmospheric testing (for oxygen, toxic gases, and flammability) and a valid entry permit.

question: For a high-pressure power plant, the preferred boiler is a watertube design because it:

options.B: It takes high pressure and steams quickly
options.C: It needs no operating controls whatsoever
options.D: It is the cheapest to build

explanation: Watertube boilers withstand high pressures safely because small-diameter tubes handle stress better than large shells, and they have rapid steaming capability due to smaller water volume per unit area.

question: Steam separators are installed in the steam drum to:

options.A: Remove droplets so drier steam leaves
options.D: Add moisture back into the live steam

explanation: Steam separators (or scrubbers) use mechanical forces to remove entrained moisture droplets from steam before it leaves the drum.

question: The heat that turns boiling water into steam at constant temperature is the:

options.A: The latent heat of ice fusion

explanation: Latent heat of vaporization is the energy absorbed to change a liquid into vapor at a constant saturation temperature.

question: To measure flow with the least permanent pressure loss, the best primary element is a:
explanation: Venturi tubes feature smooth converging and diverging cones that recover most of the pressure drop, resulting in significantly lower permanent pressure loss than an orifice plate.

question: A boiler in which the steam pressure does not exceed 100 kPa is classed as a:
explanation: Low-pressure steam heating boilers operate at pressures not exceeding 100 kPa (15 psi).

question: A higher pipe schedule number indicates a pipe with a:
explanation: Pipe schedule numbers designate standardized wall thicknesses for a given nominal size; higher schedules mean thicker walls to handle higher pressures.

question: A seal weld is applied to:

options.B: Carry the whole pressure load on its own
options.D: Prevent leakage, not carry the full load

explanation: Seal welds are non-structural welds applied exclusively to prevent leakage across threaded or mechanical joints.

question: Supplying slightly more air than the theoretical (stoichiometric) amount:

options.C: Helps ensure all the fuel is burned

explanation: A controlled amount of excess air ensures complete combustion by making certain every particle of fuel contacts sufficient oxygen.

question: To find the construction rules for a high-pressure steam boiler, an engineer consults ASME BPVC:
explanation: ASME BPVC Section I covers the rules for the construction of power boilers.

question: Carbon dioxide from fuel combustion is of concern because it:

options.B: It is highly toxic even in traces
options.C: It can be used as a fuel
options.D: It adds to the greenhouse effect

explanation: Carbon dioxide is a major greenhouse gas contributing to global climate change.

question: A check valve automatically:
explanation: A check valve is a non-return valve designed to permit fluid flow in only one direction and prevent backflow.

question: With DC electrode negative (straight polarity), most of the arc heat is at the:

options.B: At the electrode, giving faster melt-off
options.D: Within the welding electrode supply cable

explanation: With DC electrode negative (straight polarity), electrons flow from the electrode to the workpiece, concentrating about two-thirds of the heat on the workpiece.

question: A pressure gauge reads 900 kPa. The approximate absolute pressure is:
explanation: Absolute pressure equals gauge pressure plus standard atmospheric pressure ($900 \text{ kPa} + 101.3 \text{ kPa} \approx 1001 \text{ kPa}$).

question: Personal protective equipment for grinding includes, at minimum:
explanation: Grinding operations create flying particles and sparks, requiring proper eye and face protection (such as safety glasses and a face shield) at minimum.

question: Primary air in an oil burner is the air that:

options.A: Preheats the incoming boiler feedwater before entry
options.D: Mixes with fuel at the burner to start combustion

explanation: Primary air is mixed directly with the fuel at the burner nozzle to initiate and shape the flame envelope.

question: A steam pressure gauge is protected from the hot steam by installing a:
explanation: A pigtail siphon holds a pool of condensate that shields the delicate internal Bourdon tube mechanism from direct high-temperature steam.

question: Combustion air can be warmed before it reaches the burner by installing a/an:

options.A: Air heater in the flue-gas path
options.B: A deaerator on the steam main

explanation: An air heater uses waste heat from flue gases leaving the boiler to preheat incoming combustion air.

question: More boiler heating surface generally allows the boiler to:

options.B: Hold a far smaller volume of boiler water
options.D: Transfer more heat and make more steam

explanation: An increased heating surface area improves heat transfer effectiveness from combustion gases to water, increasing steam production capacity.

question: One pascal of pressure is equal to:
explanation: The Pascal (Pa) is defined as one Newton of force applied uniformly over an area of one square metre ($1 \text{ Pa} = 1 \text{ N/m}^2$).

question: Nitrogen oxides (NOx) form in a furnace mainly because of:
explanation: Thermal NOx forms when atmospheric nitrogen and oxygen combine at elevated peak flame temperatures within the furnace.

question: Flue gas leaving a boiler at a high temperature represents wasted heat that can be recovered by adding a/an:

options.B: A second, larger boiler safety valve

explanation: An economizer captures waste heat from high-temperature flue gas to preheat boiler feedwater before it enters the drum.

question: Heat transfer that needs no material medium and travels as electromagnetic waves is:
explanation: Thermal radiation transfers energy via electromagnetic waves and requires no physical medium or matter.

question: The heat needed to raise 30 kg of water by 40°C is (c = 4.2 kJ/kg·°C):
explanation: $Q = m \times c \times \Delta T = 30 \text{ kg} \times 4.2 \text{ kJ/(kg}\cdot^\circ\text{C)} \times 40^\circ\text{C} = 5040 \text{ kJ}$.

question: If a boiler's water level disappears below the gauge glass and cannot be safely restored, the operator should:
explanation: An unobservable low water level creates severe overheating risks; the operator must immediately perform an emergency burner shutdown.

question: A transformer with more turns on the secondary than on the primary will:
explanation: A step-up transformer has more secondary turns than primary turns, increasing the output alternating voltage.

question: The voltage produced by a thermocouple depends on:
explanation: Thermocouples generate a voltage proportional to the temperature difference between the measuring junction and the reference junction (Seebeck effect).

question: A safety valve is set at 1000 kPa. The pressure gauge dial should be graduated to about:
explanation: Boiler pressure gauges are typically selected to have a maximum scale reading of approximately 1.5 to 2 times the safety valve set pressure ($1000 \text{ kPa} \times 2 = 2000 \text{ kPa}$).

question: A long straight run of hot steam pipe needs an expansion loop or joint to:

options.C: Raise the working pressure of the steam
options.D: Absorb thermal growth and avoid stress

explanation: Expansion loops and flexible joints absorb dimensional changes caused by high temperature variations, preventing mechanical stress and pipe distortion.

question: A transformer has 100 primary turns and 400 secondary turns. With 110 V on the primary, the secondary voltage is:
explanation: $V_s = V_p \times (N_s / N_p) = 110 \text{ V} \times (400 / 100) = 440 \text{ V}$.

question: Alternating current (AC) is preferred for power distribution mainly because it:

options.C: It transforms easily to higher or lower voltage
options.D: It flows steadily in just one fixed direction only

explanation: AC voltage can be easily stepped up using transformers for efficient high-voltage, low-current long-distance transmission, and stepped down safely for use.

question: A soot blower is used to:

options.A: Clean ash and soot off the fireside surfaces
options.C: Strip dissolved oxygen from the boiler feedwater

explanation: Soot blowers use high-pressure steam or air jets to blast accumulated ash and soot deposits off fireside tube surfaces to maintain heat transfer efficiency.

question: Warm air rising from a radiator and cooler air falling to replace it is an example of:
explanation: Natural convection involves heat transfer through the buoyancy-driven bulk movement of fluids (such as warm air rising and cool air sinking).

question: A 50 m steam line heats by 120°C. With a coefficient of expansion of 0.000012 per °C, it expands about:
explanation: Linear expansion $\Delta L = L_0 \times \alpha \times \Delta T = 50000 \text{ mm} \times 0.000012 / ^\circ\text{C} \times 120^\circ\text{C} = 72 \text{ mm}$.

question: Machine guards are fitted to rotating equipment to:

options.C: Keep people clear of moving parts

explanation: Machine guards act as physical barriers protecting personnel from accidental contact with rotating shafts, belts, and pulleys.

question: A hot-work permit must be obtained before:
explanation: A hot-work permit system controls spark-producing operations like welding, cutting, or brazing in areas where fire hazards exist.

question: A boiler stack giving off dark smoke usually indicates:
explanation: Dark smoke from a stack is caused by unburned carbon particles, signaling incomplete combustion due to insufficient air or poor mixing.

question: Across Canadian provinces, boiler and pressure-vessel safety is administered by:

options.D: Just one single federal agency only

explanation: Responsibility for boiler design registration, inspection, and operator certification falls under provincial safety authorities (such as ABSA in Alberta).

question: Saturated steam, unlike superheated steam, may:
explanation: Saturated steam exists at the boiling point corresponding to its pressure and frequently carries entrained liquid water droplets, unlike dry superheated steam.

question: Furnace water-wall tubes serve mainly to:

options.B: Carry the feedwater over to the deaerator
options.D: Absorb radiant heat and shield the walls

explanation: Water-wall tubes line the interior furnace boundaries, absorbing intense radiant heat from combustion to generate steam while protecting refractory walls.

question: A thermowell is used with a temperature sensor to:

options.B: Protect the sensor and allow its removal
options.C: Generate a small electrical voltage signal

explanation: A thermowell acts as a protective housing sleeve, shielding temperature sensors from corrosive, high-pressure process fluids while allowing sensor replacement without draining the system.

question: A boiler burns 600 kg/h of fuel needing 15 kg of air per kg of fuel. The combustion air required is:
explanation: Total air required = $\text{Fuel consumption rate} \times \text{Air-fuel ratio} = 600 \text{ kg/h} \times 15 \text{ kg air/kg fuel} = 9000 \text{ kg/h}$.

question: A force of 8000 N acts uniformly over an area of 0.4 m². The pressure is:
explanation: Pressure = $\text{Force} / \text{Area} = 8000 \text{ N} / 0.4 \text{ m}^2 = 20,000 \text{ Pa}$.

question: The work done by a 350 N force acting over a distance of 6 m is:
explanation: Work = $\text{Force} \times \text{Distance} = 350 \text{ N} \times 6 \text{ m} = 2100 \text{ J}$ (Joules).

question: A boiler has 150 tubes, each 4 m long with a 0.06 m outside diameter. The approximate total tube heating surface (π × d × L × n) is:
explanation: Heating surface area = $\pi \times \text{diameter} \times \text{length} \times \text{number of tubes} = 3.1416 \times 0.06 \text{ m} \times 4 \text{ m} \times 150 \approx 113.1 \text{ m}^2$.

question: An operator who notices an unusual vibration during a shift should:

options.A: Record it and tell the next shift at handover
options.D: Quietly erase and rewrite the earlier log entries

explanation: Documenting abnormal operating conditions in the log and clearly communicating them during shift handover ensures operational safety and continuity.

question: A dyke or berm built around a storage tank acts as:

options.B: An inline flow-measuring orifice plate meter
options.C: Secondary containment for leaks or spills

explanation: Secondary containment structures (like berms and dikes) capture and contain hazardous liquids in the event of a tank leak, spill, or rupture.

question: A machine is a device that receives energy and uses it to:
explanation: Machines are mechanical devices designed to receive input energy and transform it to perform useful work.

question: A watertube boiler is one in which:

options.A: Water and steam are inside the tubes
options.B: Hot gas runs inside the tubes
options.C: There is no furnace at all
options.D: The shell holds all of the boiler water

explanation: In a watertube boiler, water and steam circulate inside the tubes while hot combustion gases pass across the outside of the tubes.

question: A pulley system lifts a 2000 N load with an effort of 250 N. Its mechanical advantage is:
explanation: Mechanical Advantage = $\text{Load} / \text{Effort} = 2000 \text{ N} / 250 \text{ N} = 8$.

question: Where flow must be finely throttled or regulated, the preferred valve is a:
explanation: Globe valves provide excellent flow regulation and throttling capabilities due to the disk and seat design which changes flow area progressively.

question: Self-inductance in an AC coil:

options.B: Drops the electrical resistance to almost zero
options.C: Opposes current changes even at low resistance
options.D: Only has an effect on DC

explanation: Self-inductance induces a back-EMF that opposes any changes in current (inductive reactance) within an AC circuit.

question: Shielded metal arc welding (SMAW) is also commonly known as:
explanation: Shielded metal arc welding (SMAW) uses a flux-coated consumable electrode and is widely referred to as stick welding.

question: To put out a fire, at least one element of the fire triangle must be:
explanation: Extinguishing a fire requires eliminating or removing at least one component of the fire triangle (fuel, oxygen, or heat).

question: After firetube boiler tubes are rolled (expanded) into the tubesheet, their projecting ends are:

options.A: Completely coated over with a refractory lining
options.B: Beaded over to shield them from the hot gases

explanation: The projecting ends of firetube boiler tubes are often beaded over to prevent the tube ends from overheating and burning away in the high-temperature gas stream.

question: ASME BPVC Section IV applies to:
explanation: ASME BPVC Section IV provides the rules for the construction of heating boilers (low-pressure steam and hot water boilers).

question: A motor does 9000 J of work in 45 seconds. Its power output is:
explanation: Power = $\text{Work} / \text{Time} = 9000 \text{ J} / 45 \text{ s} = 200 \text{ W}$ (Watts).

question: Adding heat that raises a substance's temperature without changing its state adds:
explanation: Sensible heat causes a measurable change in temperature without altering the physical state of the substance.

question: Short stays that support closely spaced flat surfaces, such as a firebox waterleg, are called:
explanation: Staybolts are short, threaded stay elements used to tie flat or closely spaced parallel plates together against internal pressure.

question: A fan that pushes combustion air into the furnace under positive pressure is a:
explanation: A forced-draft (FD) fan handles ambient air and forces it under positive pressure through the burner into the furnace.

question: A Canadian Registration Number (CRN) shows that:

options.B: A finished weld has passed its inspection

explanation: A CRN indicates that the design of a boiler, pressure vessel, or fitting has been officially reviewed and registered for use in a Canadian province or territory.

question: During arc welding, the eyes and skin must be shielded from:
explanation: The electric arc emits intense ultraviolet (UV) and infrared radiation capable of causing severe skin burns and arc eye.

question: A welder choosing DC electrode positive (reverse polarity) is most likely doing:

options.A: Only flat, shallow surface welds on thin plate
options.C: Overhead welds needing deep, quick penetration

explanation: With DC electrode positive (reverse polarity), more heat is concentrated at the workpiece, making it ideal for applications requiring good penetration such as out-of-position welds.

question: To capture fly ash and dust from flue gas before the stack, a plant installs a:

options.B: A spring-loaded boiler safety relief valve

explanation: Baghouses and electrostatic precipitators are specialized particulate control equipment used to clean flue gases before atmospheric discharge.

question: For complete combustion, the fuel and air need time, temperature, and:
explanation: The three T's of combustion are Time, Temperature, and Turbulence (thorough mixing of fuel and air).

question: To reduce sulphur-oxide emissions from a boiler, the most direct step is to:
explanation: Sulphur dioxide emissions are directly dependent on the sulphur content of the fuel; burning low-sulphur fuel directly minimizes these emissions.

question: Before a worker repairs a pump, the energy sources are locked and tagged. This procedure:

options.A: Periodically tests the safety relief valve
options.C: Stops the pump being started accidentally

explanation: Lockout/tagout procedures ensure that machinery is completely de-energized and protected against accidental startup during maintenance.

question: A voltage of 120 V is applied across a 30 $\Omega$ resistor. The current is:
explanation: Current ($I$) = $V / R = 120 \text{ V} / 30 \, \Omega = 4 \text{ A}$.

question: The device that admits feedwater to keep the drum at the correct level is the:
explanation: The feedwater regulator automatically controls the supply rate of makeup water to maintain a constant water level in the boiler drum.

question: A vertical firetube boiler would most appropriately be selected for:

options.C: A very large central utility power generating plant
options.D: Small low-pressure load with little floor space

explanation: Vertical firetube boilers have a compact footprint, making them ideal for small-scale, low-pressure applications with limited floor space.

question: By Bernoulli's principle, as a fluid speeds up through a restriction, its static pressure:
explanation: Bernoulli's principle states that an increase in the speed of a fluid occurs simultaneously with a decrease in static pressure.

question: If the pressure on water is increased, its boiling (saturation) temperature will:
explanation: Raising the pressure on water increases the boiling point temperature required to turn it into steam.

question: For a boiler pressure part requiring strength and weldability at high temperature, the usual material is:
explanation: Carbon steel offers the mechanical strength, toughness, and weldability required for high-temperature and high-pressure boiler construction.

question: The commutator and brushes of a DC machine:

options.B: Carry current to and from the armature
options.C: Measure the rotational speed of the shaft

explanation: The commutator and stationary carbon brushes act as a mechanical rectifier, transferring current into or out of the rotating armature windings.

question: In Ohm's law, current is equal to:
explanation: According to Ohm's law, current ($I$) equals voltage ($V$) divided by resistance ($R$).

question: A deadweight tester is used to:
explanation: A deadweight tester uses precision calibrated weights acting on a known piston area to generate exact pressures for calibrating pressure gauges.

question: Compared with a watertube boiler, a firetube boiler is limited to lower pressures because:

options.B: It has far too many small tubes packed tightly into the shell
options.C: It cannot be insulated at all
options.D: Its large shell and flat surfaces resist pressure poorly

explanation: Firetube boilers use large-diameter shells and flat stayeds surfaces that cannot withstand very high internal pressures as safely as small-diameter cylindrical tubes.

question: Steam is raised above its saturation temperature in a:
explanation: A superheater adds heat to saturated steam away from direct contact with water, raising its temperature above the saturation point.

question: Gauge pressure differs from absolute pressure in that gauge pressure:

options.C: Typically expressed as a negative value

explanation: Gauge pressure measures pressure relative to local atmospheric pressure (taking atmospheric pressure as zero).

question: A remote drum-level transmitter suddenly reads incorrectly on start-up most likely because:

options.A: The fuel being fired is wet
options.B: Reference leg has not yet filled with condensate
options.D: The whole boiler has become dangerously over-pressured

explanation: Differential pressure water level columns and transmitters require a full condensation head in the reference leg to provide accurate level readings on startup.

question: To confirm that a finished weld has no hidden internal cracks, an inspector uses:
explanation: Non-destructive examination (NDE) methods such as radiography (X-rays) or ultrasonic testing are used to detect internal flaws and cracks inside welds.

question: A boiler with a MAWP of 800 kPa is hydrostatically tested at 1.5 times the MAWP, which is:
explanation: Hydrostatic test pressure = $800 \text{ kPa} \times 1.5 = 1200 \text{ kPa}$.

question: Heavy fuel oil must be heated before it reaches the burner so that it:
explanation: Heating heavy fuel oil reduces its viscosity, allowing it to flow smoothly through piping and atomize effectively at the burner nozzle.

question: On an outside-screw-and-yoke (OS&Y) valve, the position of the disc is shown by:
explanation: An OS&Y valve features a stem that rises and lowers as the handwheel is turned, giving a clear visual indication of whether the valve is open or closed.
